text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Swedish Telecom group L.M. Ericsson is to enlarge its Danish unit with 235 new employees, saying that Denmark is well suited for developing high technology software because of its highly qualified technicians.

--- Denmark's third largest bank, BG Bank, which was formed in a merger of Bikuben and Girobank, is to end a programme of low interest rates for 500,000 former Giro bank customers, changing its strategy of running the Girobank part of BG Bank as a budget operation under the name of Netbank.

--- Telecom group Tele Danmark is to alter its offer of discounts on long evening domestic calls after the consumer council said that the campaign was misleading and did not give consumers the promised discounts.
--- Deposits to pension savings accounts set new records in 1996, with 45 billion crowns paid in, compared to 38 billion crowns the year before.
--- Danish bonds produced good returns in 1996, but profits in 1997 may be reduced by two thirds, Denmark's largest bank Den Danske Bank estimates.
